check: how the 24h run terminates, and whether it can end early or hang
why: Two opposite failures were possible: stopping before the window because the queue drained, or never stopping because refills kept arriving. The termination logic needed reading to tell them apart.
mechanism: tick() refills only when pending and inFlight are both empty AND the window has not elapsed, so a refill is impossible once the window closes.
tick() calls stop() when pending and inFlight are both empty, which after the window closes is reached naturally as the last work completes.
windowElapsed() compares elapsed seconds against config.durationSeconds(), using the same startedWallNanos origin the refill log reports, so the log line and the decision cannot disagree.
earlyStopIsImpossible: Before the window closes, an empty queue triggers a refill rather than a stop, which is what the nine observed refills demonstrate. The queue has twice been empty and both times work resumed.
hangIsImpossible: After the window closes, no new work can be queued, so pending and inFlight can only decrease. The drain then completes and stop() fires.
observedAgreement: The refill log lines report remainingSeconds counting down from 86400, and the latest reads 72143 at 14257 elapsed. Those are the same arithmetic as windowElapsed, so the logged countdown is the termination condition rather than a separate display.
